record.paper_title: Report from the Open Problems Session at OPSFA13
record.original_question: Can one create easy-to-use software that, for a general family of orthogonal polynomials specified for example by a weight function, returns uniform asymptotic expansions together with error bounds, so that non-experts can reliably use these asymptotics in applications such as quadrature and fast transforms?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to make uniform asymptotics with error bounds easy-to-use, for general orthogonal polynomials? ... A software package that would take in a general weight and return the uniform asymptotic expansion would be ideal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop an easy-to-use software package addressing the following problem. Given as input a weight function $w:I\to[0,\infty)$ on an interval $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ (subject to mild regularity assumptions sufficient to guarantee existence of orthogonal polynomials of all degrees and the relevant asymptotic regimes), let $\{p_n(x;w)\}_{n\ge 0}$ denote the sequence of polynomials orthonormal with respect to $w$, i.e.
$$\int_I p_n(x;w)\,p_m(x;w)\,w(x)\,dx=\delta_{nm}.$$
The package should automatically produce, for arbitrary $n$ and arbitrary $x$ (including bulk, edge/turning-point, and exterior regions), a uniform asymptotic expansion
$$p_n(x;w)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1} A_k(n,x)+R_K(n,x),$$
together with an explicit, rigorously valid error bound $|R_K(n,x)|\le E_K(n,x)$ that holds uniformly on the specified region of $(n,x)$. The construction must be carried out for a general family of weights (rather than a fixed classical family), and the output must be in a form directly usable in numerical applications such as Gauss-type quadrature and fast orthogonal-polynomial transforms.

Question: Is it possible to design and implement such a package — taking in a general weight $w$ and returning uniform asymptotic expansions of $p_n(\cdot;w)$ together with rigorous, computable error bounds valid uniformly across all relevant regions — so that it can be reliably used by non-experts?
artifact.status_search_result: Existing software (e.g., ORTHPOL and related packages) generates recurrence coefficients, zeros, and Gauss-type quadrature rules for orthogonal polynomials with respect to arbitrary weights, and there is substantial theoretical work on uniform asymptotics with error bounds (e.g., Riemann–Hilbert based results for varying exponential weights, Levin–Lubinsky bounds). However, no unified, easy-to-use package that ingests a general weight and outputs uniform asymptotic expansions together with rigorous error bounds appears to exist; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Algorithm 726: ORTHPOL
status_evidence.snippet: Package generates recurrence coefficients and Gauss-type quadrature rules for orthogonal polynomials with respect to arbitrary weights.
status_evidence.claim: Existing general-weight software focuses on recurrence coefficients and quadrature, not uniform asymptotic expansions with error bounds.

status_evidence.title: Bounds and Asymptotics for Orthogonal Polynomials for Varying Weights
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes bounds and asymptotics under almost minimal conditions on varying weights.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical uniform asymptotics with bounds exist for broad weight classes, but only as mathematical results, not implemented as a turnkey package.
